citations.claim: just before violation still penetrating but within limit
progressive sink: penetration increasing each step
approach speed ~9.46 m/s leftward, controller at fmax

counterfactual.change: disabled controller (enabled true->false, one field); without sustained fmax push the same body/wall geometry no longer penetrates, proving controller force overpowering contact correction is the cause

explanation: Controller-driven hover body (ignores gravity) is pushed left at ~9.3 m/s with sustained fmax=42.95 N into a thin wall (w=0.346). Collision positional correction/impulse is insufficient to repel the controller force, so the body gradually sinks through the wall side/top corner: distance_to_surface goes from -0.062 at step 350 to -0.100 at 351 to -0.138 at 352 to -0.175 at 353, exceeding 0.15 limit. With only 2 substeps per step (dt~0.004), per-substep displacement ~0.019 m allows progressive interpenetration rather than a single tunneling event, indicating force-biased integration outruns contact resolution.
vision_note: The red controller-driven body is driven left toward the green waypoint and makes contact with the top corner of the thin vertical grey wall. From step 350 to 353 it is not repelled and instead progressively sinks into the wall, with the circle visibly overlapping the wall's top edge more each frame.
